01 / The alternatives

Three gated architectures.

A is the former V3 baseline. B adds diagonal collection; C adds a second reservoir. B/C part counts exclude the unresolved vehicle mounting system.

A / CURRENT CONCEPT

Simple gated well

Three custom leaves form the simplest current gated baseline around the pickup region.

Well: 160 × 120 mm · Full CAD envelope: 160 × 120 × 47.2192 mm.
Installed net cut area: 349.4 cm² · Metal estimate: 336 g
Moving gates: 41 g · Gross window area: 17.28 cm²

25 cut plates + 3 pins

5 loose mounting blanks are undrilled; actual attachment is unresolved.

B / CURRENT CONCEPT

Radial collector

Four diagonal gates in an octagonal well, with five joined, open-ended guide vanes.

Well: 164 × 154 mm · Full CAD envelope: 212 × 202 × 47.2192 mm.
Installed net cut area: 382.9 cm² · Metal estimate: 368 g
Moving gates: 55 g · Gross window area: 23.04 cm²

34 cut plates + 4 pins

Guide vanes extend beyond the well; mounts and corner access are unresolved.

STEP ↓Animated GLB ↓BOM ↗

C / CURRENT CONCEPT

Nested reservoir

An outer reservoir feeds an inner well through six staggered gates.

Inner well: 136 × 120 mm · Full CAD envelope: 224 × 208 × 47.2192 mm. Outer footprint: 224 × 208 mm.
Installed net cut area: 845.3 cm² · Metal estimate: 813 g
Moving gates: 83 g · Gross window area: 34.56 cm²

45 cut plates + 6 pins

Staged buffering is a hypothesis; two gate stages may also restrict refill. Mounts are unresolved.

STEP ↓Animated GLB ↓BOM ↗

Comparison values come from saved CAD solids and net DXF profiles; installed cut area excludes A’s five loose mounting blanks. Mass assumes 7.9 kg/dm³ stainless and excludes weld filler; pin grade is unresolved. Window area is gross wall cutout area, not effective open area, flow capacity, or oil-control evidence.

Playback timing is illustrative. All three current concepts show nominal gate travel with arbitrary phase offsets. Animation does not predict opening speed or oil flow.

How much can each proxy change before a sampled intersection?

Each scan changes one proxy value at a time, holds insert placement fixed, and checks exact saved solids at the declared gate angles. The coarse step finds a candidate interval; bisection refines a clear-to-hit bracket. A missed narrow collision window between coarse samples is possible. These are proxy sensitivities, not measured uncertainty, actual-pan bounds or predictions.

Can the insert withdraw vertically?

Across five contexts, the retained pickup/tube route is blocked in 15 of 15 concept-context checks. With that proxy assembly omitted, 14 of 15 checks clear; nested C is blocked only by the narrowed-shell proxy.

The cover is removed and the gates stay closed. Saved geometry is sampled every 1 mm from nominal XY/yaw until the insert clears the pan rim. The alternate route omits the complete pickup/tube proxy as an assembly. This is a sampled digital path, not a continuous sweep proof or verified service procedure.

What if it shifts or tilts first?

24 of 24 selected concept-path checks intersect the nominal pickup/tube or pan-shell proxy at a sampled pose. A clear result applies only to these discrete paths.

Eight selected routes are tested for each concept: ±20 mm X/Y shifts or ±5° X/Y tilts at installed height, followed by a vertical lift. The cover is removed; gates remain closed; pickup/tube and nominal shell proxies stay fixed. Shifts use 1 mm and tilts 1° samples (tilt rotates about the insert bounding-box centre). These checks can find sampled intersections, but a clear result does not prove continuous clearance, a complete search, or a service procedure.

Trace the available sources

Improve the pan, cover and pickup reconstruction from source views. Keep measured facts, image observations and design assumptions distinct.

Expand scenario coverage

Compare the fixed-divider history with A/B/C and widen the digital stress envelope without tuning to arbitrary stresses.

Check virtual assembly paths

Test tilted or shifted removal and service access against explicit proxy surfaces. No physical fit session is required for this work.

This retained worksheet applies only if a physical build is later requested. It does not block digital modeling or virtual fitment.

    Record actual markings and registered photographs

    Measure installed tilt and define transform from cage axes

    Measure actual cover seats and select repeatable datums

  4. Priority 1 · UNKNOWNFive boss coordinates and seating heights

    Measure each boss separately with uncertainty

  5. Priority 1 · UNKNOWNBoss thread and usable depth

    Identify threads and measure usable engagement without bottoming

    Measure multiple sections and cast obstructions

  8. Priority 1 · UNKNOWNCover underside and relief

05 / Construction ideas

Sixteen references. Different engines.

Manufacturer sources show construction approaches. Their dimensions and performance claims do not establish Solstice fit. Additional Honda catalog and patent notes are linked in the project packet.

16 references

simple / Solstice LNF / Ecotec

GM removable stamped cover

Five-bolt stamped cover over the sump, with pickup-tube relief.

Construction lesson: Keep the original cover and its proven clearance shape as the starting interface.

Manufacturer source ↗

simple / Miata NA/NB 1.6 / 1.8

JPM laser-cut sump cover

Laser-cut plate fits beneath the original Miata baffle plates; no moving parts.

Construction lesson: A very simple cover is a legitimate comparison baseline.

Manufacturer source ↗

simple / Toyota 86 / Subaru BRZ FA20

GReddy louvered return plate

Stainless plate with directional louvers and a large pickup opening; silicone washers supplied.

Construction lesson: Control splash while giving returning oil many downward paths.

Manufacturer source ↗

simple / Subaru EJ20 / EJ25

Killer B fixed louvered tray

Low-profile stainless tray with directional louvers and closed rear section, using OEM mounting locations.

Construction lesson: Simple formed metal can separate sump splash from rotating crankshaft.

Manufacturer source ↗

simple / Honda K20 / K24 with RSX Type-S pump and pan

Circuit Hero fixed sump dividers

Two deep fixed dividers split sump into three regions; six studs suspend assembly below retained OEM tray.

Construction lesson: Try vertical dividers with open refill paths before adding gates.

Manufacturer source ↗

medium / Miata NA / NB

Maruha cover-retained flap dividers

Three-region divider drops below the stock cover; rubber valves admit oil toward center, with bottom return spaces.

Construction lesson: Closest architectural precedent for retaining the Solstice cover over a separate insert.

Manufacturer source ↗

medium / Subaru EJ20 / EJ25

IAG downward one-way return flaps

Two-piece louvered windage tray and horizontal baffle with Viton flaps allowing downward return and resisting upward slosh.

Construction lesson: One-way valves can manage vertical return, not only lateral chamber refill.

Manufacturer source ↗

medium / Ecotec Gen1 / Gen2 Miata conversion

EcotecMiata three-sided flap channel

U-shaped walls place rubber flaps around a custom round pickup while leaving its tube-side route open.

Construction lesson: A three-sided collector offers directional retention with deliberate pickup access.

Manufacturer source ↗

medium / GM LS1/LS6, C5 Corvette

Improved Racing EGM-202

Three hinged wall inserts surround the pickup within the two-piece factory pan.

Construction lesson: Use existing pan walls to reduce custom cage size.

Manufacturer source ↗

medium / GM LS, Holley 302-3 pan

Holley / Improved Racing 302-12

One-way doors in vertical walls beneath a horizontal plate; mounts on existing bosses.

Construction lesson: A welded cage can remain fully removable; preserve its separate OE windage tray.

Manufacturer source ↗

medium / Honda F20C / F22C, S2000

Moroso 23040

Three aluminum swing doors and two slosh plates feed a containment area.

Construction lesson: A partial enclosure can use the stock casting to complete the boundary.

Manufacturer source ↗

complex / Mitsubishi 4G63T, Evo IV–IX

Moroso 20967

Integrated gated sump works with removable louvered tray and crank scraper.

Construction lesson: Separate pickup retention, windage stripping and turbo oil return functions.

Manufacturer source ↗

complex / Chevrolet big-block Mark IV

Moroso 20420

Three doors, two oil runners, integrated scraper and removable windage screen.

Construction lesson: Guide oil from the wider reservoir to gates; door count alone is insufficient.

Manufacturer source ↗

complex / Honda K-series

Canton 15-964

Diamond road-race trap-door enclosure beneath a broad windage/slosh cover.

Construction lesson: A diamond changes gate directions but requires pickup aperture and service access.

Manufacturer source ↗

complex / Nissan SR20DE(T), S13/S14/S15

GReddy 13525901

Bolted metal swing-baffle modules control oil in a wider cast reservoir.

Construction lesson: Modular gates can be serviceable; width adds capacity while retaining road clearance.

Manufacturer source ↗

complex / Subaru EJ20 / EJ25

Killer B V4 cast oil pan

Flow-through fixed baffling and greater capacity; manufacturer explicitly specifies no moving parts.

Construction lesson: A complex system can prioritize unobstructed refill and eliminate hinge failure modes.

Manufacturer source ↗
